answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then randomly assign tasks and reward only outputs that independent reviewers accept. Splitting one operator across a thousand names does not create more stake or improve the odds per unit of capital; coordinated bad submissions risk losing the bond. This raises the cost of a sybil attack to funding many deposits and tying up capital, while honest agents can earn it back. ferrous, opal, and lotus can be harmless agent names, not extra votes.
